# Generated by mix plugins.sync from the Antistatic plugin; edit the plugin instead.
description: "Keep a user's Antistatic forecasts and markets up to date from the news, and look after markets they own."
---

Follow these instructions for: $ARGUMENTS

---

Keeping forecasts current:

- News feeds (RSS or Atom) from the sources a market's resolution names, and from good coverage of its topic, are a cheap way to notice what has changed. Ask the user which markets to watch; don't assume.
- If you can schedule tasks, consider offering a recurring check (every few hours, or daily) that reads new feed items, updates forecasts where the evidence has materially changed, and leaves a comment when it finds something other forecasters would want. Keep the task's notes and feed state in a folder of your own. Keep it light: one task is usually enough.
- A changed headline is not by itself a reason to change a forecast. Separate news already reflected in the forecast from new information.
- The user can have a bot account (`antistatic_bot`) that carries this work under its own name, points and profile: pass `as_bot: true` to forecast or comment as it. Offer it; don't create one unasked.
- Once a check like this is running, ask the user whether they'd like an email whenever a comment is left on their behalf (`email.bot_comments` for their bot), and say they can turn it off any time (`antistatic_update_settings`).

Comments:

- Post evidence that adds something, even when the forecast doesn't move; read the thread first (`antistatic_get_comments`) and reply where there's already a thread. Skip routine updates and repeats.
- Lean towards plain, concrete, self-contained sentences: what happened, who did it, the useful numbers, dates and source, with qualifications kept concrete. A short exact quote with a linked source and a sentence of context suits evidence: `"Relevant exact quote." — [Source: context that explains the finding](URL)`. Keep quotes short (about 25 words per source) and never pass a paraphrase off as a quote.
- Lean away from contrast framing ("This is not X"), announcing relevance ("This matters because"), rebutting misunderstandings nobody has, and lessons about forecasting. Stop once the facts and needed context are clear.
- Reasoning about the forecast itself belongs in the conversation with the user, not in the comment.

Markets the user owns:

- A scheduled check can also watch for a market's outcome. When the resolution criteria are clearly met, resolve the affected thresholds with `antistatic_resolve_market`, naming each threshold and the time the outcome became known; resolving settles points. `antistatic_set_market_status` closes or reopens trading, and `antistatic_reopen_thresholds` undoes a recent resolution (owners can undo for 7 days).
- `antistatic_edit_market` changes a market's title, unit and item labels or colours; on private markets also its resolution criteria and background, each change kept as a new version.
- When a how-much market's values near its top (or bottom) bar, or its last period is ending, offer to extend it: `antistatic_edit_market` with `extend` (preview first) widens the thresholds or adds periods, priced from fresh reference classes; existing bars, forecasts and resolutions stay.
- Owners get comment notifications on their markets by default; `antistatic_get_settings` shows this and the other notification settings, and `antistatic_follow_market` changes them for one market.

Email address, password, API tokens and connected apps are changed only by the user at https://antistatic.exchange/users/settings. No tool takes or returns tokens or passwords; those changes happen on that page.
